conditions.label: S-posture
conditions.consequence: An exaggerated low-back arch at address pre-tensions the lower back and makes it harder to turn the pelvis without the spine taking the load.

provenance.searchTerms: lumbar extension hip range of motion golfers

conditions.injuryNote: A sustained end-range low-back arch under rotational load has been investigated as a contributor to lower back pain in golfers, and the findings are mixed — a systematic review found no significant difference in hip angle, trunk angle or crunch factor between recreational golfers with and without pain. Treat it as a loading pattern worth knowing about rather than a demonstrated risk. Worth raising with a clinician if pain is present.

conditions.label: Trail hip hike
conditions.consequence: The trail hip rising rather than rotating substitutes a vertical move for a turn and shortens the effective backswing. It is measured as the tilt of the hip LINE and not as the pelvis rising as a whole — one hip riding up over the other is the observation, and a pelvis that lifts evenly is a different thing with its own reading.

conditions.label: Lead knee works in at the top
conditions.consequence: The lead knee travelling in toward the trail leg — further than its own hip has travelled — is the lower body finding the FEELING of a backswing without the turn that should have produced it. What it costs is depth: the pelvis has not wound up over the trail leg, so there is less to unwind into and the downswing tends to get started by the arms and chest instead. Read this as an observation that points somewhere, not as a conclusion. A face-on camera cannot see how far the pelvis actually turned, and the same picture is produced by a golfer who turned deeply and one who barely turned at all — subtracting the hip's own travel is what separates them, and it does not separate them perfectly. A down-the-line view, or a physical hip-rotation screen, is what settles which it was.

conditions.label: Pelvis rises during the backswing
conditions.consequence: Gaining pelvis height on the way back lifts the whole swing centre before the downswing has started, and the height has to be given back on the way through for the club to reach the ball. It is the mirror of sinking into the backswing and shares its consequence: a strike whose depth changes from swing to swing rather than one that is consistently heavy or thin.

conditions.label: Face held open through impact
conditions.consequence: The lead forearm has not rotated back to where it started by impact, so the face arrives open. A BAND-AID when it is the standard swing: holding the face off is how a hook gets managed without fixing what is turning it over, and it is bought with release speed and distance every swing, not just the ones where it was wanted. That is why it is reported rather than excused — a golfer who does this on every shot is paying for a compensation they may not know they have made. Shaping a fade with it on a given shot is a choice, and so is bending a hook round a tree; the model reads one swing at a time and cannot tell either from a habit, which is the same reason `slice` and `hook` are conditions here and not styles. The mirror of the face being rolled shut on the same axis, and the two share a cause: the face is being squared by the arms rather than carried round by the body.
